chunks: Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Masroor - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Al-Hussein ibn Muhammad ibn Amer Al-Ash'ari quoted Al-Mo'ali ibn Muhammad al-Basry, on the authority of Al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Vasha, on the authority of Aban that Zurarah heard Aba Ja'far (peace be upon him) say:
Twelve Imams, among them Ali, Al-Hasan, and Al-Hussein. Then the Imams are from the progeny of Al-Hussein (peace be upon them).
And I have recorded whatever narrations I have seen on this issue in the book Kamal ad-Din va Tamam al-Ni'mat fi Isbat il-Qaybat va Kashf ul-Hayrat.
ai.seo_question: Who are the twelve Imams according to Shia tradition and what is their lineage?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq cites this chain to affirm the fixed number of twelve divinely appointed leaders, emphasizing that the lineage continues through the progeny of Imam Husayn (AS). He cross-references this with his seminal work *Kamal al-Din*, where this narration serves as a crucial proof for the doctrine of the Occultation (Ghayba) and the continuity of divine guidance despite the hidden Imam.
